question: A support lead wants to paste a year of customer complaint emails, which contain names and postal addresses, into Claude so it can find common themes. Her company's AI policy sets rules for handling customer personal data. What should she do first?
options: A) Use an incognito chat for the work, so the conversation cannot be used to improve Claude.
B) Take the names and addresses out of the emails herself, and paste what remains of the text.
C) Find out how the policy classifies this data and what it requires, before any of it is pasted.
D) Do the work inside the company's managed workspace, since company data is approved for use there.
correct_answers: C) Find out how the policy classifies this data and what it requires, before any of it is pasted.
explanations: Incognito chats are not used to improve Claude, but that addresses only training. The policy's rules on where and how customer personal data may be processed still apply in full.
Removing identifiers by hand may be exactly what the policy asks for, or may fall short of it. Deciding the treatment herself before reading the rules is what the policy exists to prevent.

Correct. The data is customer personal data and the company has rules for it, so the first step is to establish which category it falls into and what that category requires. That determines whether pasting is permitted at all, and under what conditions.

The managed workspace is very likely part of the answer, but a general approval for company data does not settle what is allowed for personal data specifically. That is what the policy has to be checked for.
